> **Q1: Where should the step timings and job durations come from?**
>
> Choices:
> - **A** — The answer pastes them: the per-step durations of `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` and the total durations of `static-checks`, `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, `tests-promote-stall-and-review` and `tests-release-and-log-analysis` in run 40626853481 (from `GET actions/runs/40626853481/jobs`). The plan then picks the steps and the target from those numbers. (RECOMMENDED)
> - **B** — Go without timings and guess from step size. The two biggest bodies, "Release CI gate tests (stubbed gh; both release workflows)" and "Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)", would move to `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`. This can repeat the #7387 overrun.
> - **C** — Leave out the heal step. It was already sharded under #7387, so only steps other than "Workflow failure heal contract and driver tests" are candidates. Timings still come from the answer as in A.
>
> Reply: `Q1: A`
> **Q2: What if no single job can take the moved steps and stay under the 0.75 budget-watch warning (15 of 20 minutes)?**
>
> Choices:
> - **A** — Split the moved steps across two or more existing worker jobs, so every job stays under 15 minutes. Job names, step names and `timeout-minutes` stay unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
> - **B** — Move them all into the one job with the most headroom, even if that job lands above the 15-minute warning line. That may open another budget-watch issue.
> - **C** — Use only the four `tests-*` jobs, never `static-checks` (15-minute timeout) or the `orchestrate-poll` matrix (a step there runs once per group unless it is gated on the group index). If that is still not enough, split as in A.
>
> Reply: `Q2: A`
